title: NIH Stroke Scale (NIHSS)
sources: Brott T, Adams HP Jr, Olinger CP, et al. Measurements of acute cerebral infarction: a clinical examination scale. Stroke. 1989;20(7):864-870
NIH Stroke Scale, National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) — training, certification, and scoring materials

Adams HP Jr, Davis PH, Leira EC, et al. Baseline NIH Stroke Scale score strongly predicts outcome after stroke: a report of the TOAST trial. Neurology. 1999;53(1):126-131 (score-to-outcome relationship)

changelog.change: Converted all 15 items from free-entry integers to select dropdowns carrying the official NIH Stroke Scale category text for each score, per user UI feedback (a fixed small scored set should be a picker, not a numeric field). Supersedes the v1 scope note about not encoding per-point criteria — these are the standardized scale's own published category labels for the score a certified examiner has already determined, not exam-technique instruction. UN (untestable — amputation/joint fusion for items 5-6, intubation for item 10) is not modeled; enter the closest scored category if genuinely untestable, per your institution's convention.

Expanded sources with the full Brott 1989 citation, the NINDS scale materials, and Adams 1999 (TOAST) for the score-to-outcome relationship; named the severity-band scheme and its alternate in notes; removed the needs-primary-source flag.
Item score ranges only, per the deliberate scope decision in Calculator_Logic_Build_Spec.md.

purpose: Standardized stroke severity — drives thrombolytic/thrombectomy eligibility and serial monitoring. Enter the item scores a trained examiner has already determined.
notes: Each item's dropdown shows the official NIH Stroke Scale category text for that score — administer the exam per NINDS-certified technique first; this tool is for entering the score you've already determined, not for teaching how to elicit it. This tool sums the item scores you enter. Severity bands shown (0 none / 1-4 minor / 5-15 moderate / 16-20 moderate-severe / 21-42 severe) follow the NINDS NIH Stroke Scale descriptors used in the scale's training materials; an alternate common scheme is < 5 / 5-14 / 15-24 / > 24. Bands are for communication and trending — thrombolytic and thrombectomy decisions use the specific trial criteria and clinical context, not a cut-point. Higher baseline score predicts worse outcome (Adams 1999): roughly ≤ 6 favors a good outcome and ≥ 16 a high probability of death or severe disability.
